title: Recovered Vera v0.5 QLoRA training, Ollama build, and identity-evaluation arc
event_time: original final-candidate training execution before or by 2026-09-01; recovery/deployment/evaluation 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-02; exact original training timestamp unresolved
provenance_ceiling: Direct repository checkpoints recover a completed final-candidate QLoRA run (`1.0.0-final-candidate`) against local SmolLM3-3B lineage, three epochs/105 steps with stable train/validation/test metrics, and adapter SHA-256 `1a2e593e2b7d018467b80792eb3f180b05b7ff83d7e508d4cd51b78ab6c73da9`. The adapter was converted to GGUF and a local Ollama `vera-v05:latest` Q4_K_M artifact was structurally created/verified. First open-ended identity smoke test failed by self-identifying as `Hedwig`; an unadapted-base control was generic, while an explicit Vera identity cue elicited Vera association, supporting prompt-sensitive/unstable identity behavior rather than a dead adapter. Later native PEFT inference using the exact recovered adapter also failed uncued Vera self-identification before GGUF/Ollama, while retaining Vera-related boundary/continuity style. Training code showed no explicit assistant/completion-only loss mask and likely optimized full serialized sequences. Current historical classification at that frontier: training numerically completed/healthy and Vera-related style learned, but stable proper-name identity insufficiently learned/retained and not inference-qualified. Two plausible upstream hypotheses remained training-objective dilution and unresolved immutable base-model lineage match.
notes: Do not treat training completion, Ollama registration, prompt-cued Vera association, or recovered adapter existence as native Vera qualification/current memory/current identity effect.
